archetypes.name: shell-api-claims
archetypes.rationale: The plan names specific shell functions (_WTR_OUT, _WTR_RC, with_transient_retry, NET_FAIL_FILES), line numbers, and Bash 3.2-safe constructs — each claim is a potential plan defect if the source diverges.
archetypes.prompt_body: Verify every plan-claimed shell function name, exported variable (e.g. _WTR_OUT, _WTR_RC, NET_FAIL_FILES, transient_envelope_predicate_none), line number reference, and mktemp pattern against the actual source files. Check that each new local declaration is safe under the script's set -u/-euo pipefail environment and that no introduced construct violates Bash 3.2 portability rules (no associative arrays, namerefs, mapfile, ${var^^}). Identify any line reference in the plan that no longer matches the current file, any variable or function name that does not exist in the claimed form, and any new construct that would fail on macOS system Bash 3.2. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.

archetypes.name: scope-exclusion
archetypes.rationale: The plan explicitly excludes two design-log-publish.sh findings as already resolved on main (#2581); if that claim is wrong the shipped change silently leaves known gaps open.
archetypes.prompt_body: Verify every out-of-scope claim in the plan against the current state of the relevant source files, particularly the assertion that FINDING_10 (design-log-publish.sh trap cleanup) and FINDING_14 (design-log-publish.sh list/view retry) were resolved by #2581 and require no code change. Check scripts/design-log-publish.sh for the list_fail_file/view_fail_file trap inclusion and the list/view with_transient_retry wrappers described in the issue. Also verify the plan's claim that no new live gh/git subcommands or flags are introduced — only wrapping — holds against each modified call site. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.

archetypes.name: test-infrastructure
archetypes.rationale: The plan prescribes specific test implementation patterns (SLEEP_SCRIPT_DIR stub, count-file flips, env-gated fake-gh branches) that must match the actual existing harness infrastructure or the new tests will be structurally broken.
archetypes.prompt_body: Verify that each test implementation pattern prescribed in the plan — SLEEP_SCRIPT_DIR no-op stub export, count-file flip conventions (GH_VIEW_COUNT_FILE, GH_CHECKS_COUNT_FILE), env-gated fake-gh failure branches, and PATH-stub git repo setup — matches how these patterns are actually implemented in the existing sibling harnesses (test-create-pr.sh, test-merge-pr.sh, test-clarify-comment.sh, test-rebase-push-*.sh). Check whether the plan's instruction to add NET_FAIL_FILES+=() entries inside recover_existing_pr_after_create_conflict() is consistent with how that EXIT-trap array is scoped and populated elsewhere in create-pr.sh. Identify any plan-described test pattern that the repo infrastructure does not support or that differs structurally in a way that would cause the new harness to fail or not exercise the intended code path. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.
